items.title: Ray Conniff interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 14, 1998
items.q: I started taking Tchaikovsky’s scores — did you ever do that?

ctx.x: How long did you hold on to that thing?

Oh boy do I wish I had that today, yeah. For one dollar, what an investment. And of course I used it for a while as a transposing device, but that led me into writing, because later on I studied and I would, I started with Hugo Friedhofer, by the way, boy he was great. Do you remember him? He wrote for the motion pictures out here on the west coast. And then I ran into, who was it, somebody tipped me off to start looking into the classics, and I started taking Tchaikovsky’s scores — did you ever do that? You take…
